thread.title: Alphabet Earnings: Shares Punished After $3 Billion Loss - Barron's

author: Jon Swartz
title: Alphabet Earnings: Shares Punished After $3 Billion Loss - Barron's
text:
Shares of Alphabet (GOOGL) tumbled 3% after it reported mixed results for its fiscal fourth quarter.
Illustration: Getty Images The company also named John Hennessy as its new chairman to replace Eric Schmidt on Feb. 15.
The good news was that revenue rose to $32.32 million from $26.06 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. But the bad news was a doozy: The company lost $3.02 billion, or $4.35 per share. A year ago, it posted a profit of $5.33 billion, or $7.56 per share.
Alphabet explained the discrepancy as the result of a $9.9 billion tax expense caused by the recent U.S. tax overhaul. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected revenue of $25.57 billion and earnings per share of $9.98.
The tax-related hiccup marred an otherwise decent quarter. Worldwide downloads on Google Play exceeded 19 billion in the last three months of 2017—the service’s best-ever showing, widening its lead over Apple 's (AAPL) iOS App Store , according to App Annie . (The number includes only new downloads and doesn’t count reinstalls or app updates.)
Baird Equity Research "sees investments in cloud and other initiatives as key long-term positives" for Alphabet, for which it has a $1,150 price target.
On Wednesday, Google said it will alter its search function to include "diverse perspectives."
